utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And I would now like to read a short summary of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Dragan Todorovic was a member of the VRS during the war. He served with various units, including a period when he served in the RS MUP Special Police Brigade's 2nd Sekovici Detachment. In late 1994, he joined the Vlasenica platoon of the VRS's 10th Sabotage Detachment based in Dragasevac, a village around 4 to 5 kilometres from Vlasenica. He worked in logistics supporting both the Vlasenica and Bijeljina platoons of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. On different occasions during the war, Todorovic encountered senior VRS officers, including the Main Staff chief of intelligence, Colonel Petar Salapura, who communicated the most with the 10th Sabotage Detachment; the Main Staff chief of security, Colonel Ljubisa Beara; and their superior, General Tolimir. Todorovic testified that he saw General Tolimir for the first time in Zepa. On the 10th of July, 1995, Todorovic's unit received a written order to prepare to deploy into the field. The order was sent in the name of Milorad Pelemis, the commander of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, but signed by Franc Kos, a fellow member. The unit packed their gear and waited for the Bijeljina platoon, then drove to Zeleni Jadar, where they spent the night. The next day, 11th of July, Commander Pelemis arrived. He ordered the unit to divide into two groups and to enter Srebrenica town. They entered the town in the afternoon without meeting any resistance and secured the police station. Todorovic saw senior officers, including General Mladic and Drina Corps commander General Milenko Zivanovic. Mladic ordered the unit to continue the blockade at the police station to secure any important documents that might be there, and then issued an order for other soldiers to move towards Potocari. General Mladic relieved the unit of its duty in Srebrenica on the evening of 11th of July. He told them to retreat and that they had 48 hours to search and take whatever they wanted. Todorovic's unit spent the night of 11th of July near Srebrenica town. On 12th of July he went with a driver to Dragasevac to prepare for the return of soldiers to the base. Later that day, as the 10th Sabotage Detachment units returned from their deployment to Srebrenica, there was a vehicle accident in which a soldier was killed. Todorovic and others were assigned to make the necessary arrangements for the soldier's body to be returned to his family in Trebinje. They travelled there on the 13th July and the soldier's funeral was on the 14th of July. The soldiers who had travelled to Trebinje arrived back at Dragasevac by around 11.00 a.m. on the 15th of July. Commander Pelemis was absent, and the troops did not have any activities to perform. Then, VRS Main Staff officer Dragomir Pecanac and Drina Corps security chief, Lieutenant Colonel Vujadin Popovic arrived. Pecanac came into the camp and asked 10th Sabotage Detachment member Zoran Obrenovic for some soldiers. Pecanac said that he had a meeting in Zvornik with Colonel Beara. Pecanac rounded up a group of soldiers and took them from the camp down the road towards Sekovici. Todorovic provided equipment and supplies to these soldiers, including zolja rocket-launchers, a machine-gun, and ammunition for automatic rifles. Todorovic saw the soldiers leaving. The group included Franc Kos, who was in charge; Boris Popov; Marko Boskic; and Drazen Erdemovic. Todorovic testified that he did not know what task the group was used for. Regarding Popovic's presence at the Dragasevac compound, Todorovic testified that the gate-keeper told him that Popovic was outside. Todorovic saw Popovic's car and could see a person inside it, however he claimed that he did not see Popovic. Todorovic was read notes of his FBI interview where he stated: "When he got back to Dragasevac, a senior officer named Popovic was also present, although he waited for Pecanac by his Volkswagen Golf outside the driveway's gate." In addition, he was read part path of his OTP interview statement in which he states that: "Between 10.00 a.m. and 12.00 noon, Major Pecanac arrived at Dragasevac with a security officer, Lieutenant Colonel, or Colonel Vujadin Popovic. They arrived in two separate seeks. Pecanac came into the compound whilst Popovic remained on the outside ... all the while, Popovic remained outside the compound area." Todorovic then admitted that he did, in fact, see Popovic that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my summary. I have just a few questions, if I may, that I would like to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, you previously testified that you saw General Tolimir for the first time in Zepa, and I want to ask you about that topic. When did you go to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We arrived in Zepa on the 20th or the 21st of June [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could you confirm the month and the year that you are talking about? In the transcript I see the 20th or 21st of June.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It was in July. It was July, the month of July, not the month of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And just for the transcript records, sir, the year as well, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: 1995. But the month is July, not June.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I believe the month is now correctly recorded in the transcript. Sir, with whom did you go to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: With my detachment, the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Since there are two platoons of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, which platoon or platoons were deployed there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I was with the Vlasenica platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did members of the Bijeljina platoon go to Zepa or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did your commander, Pelemis, deploy to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And what was the task you were deployed to in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We were supposed to be engaged in an action to take, to conquer Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And, sir, where did you travel to when you went towards Zepa? Where did you arrive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We travelled across Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And where did you make your camp? Where did you spend the night on the day you arrived in the Zepa area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We camped above Zepa on an elevation, and I don't know its name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Do you know the name of any of the villages closest to where you were deployed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And can you describe the immediate location, were there any buildings where you were, were you by a road, were you in the forest? Please give a description as best you can.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: There by the road there was a house. There was a slope, a hillside, there was a United Nations transporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And how long were you deployed to that location?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We spent the night there and the entire following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Apart from other members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, who did you see during your deployment to that area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska, units of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And was it during this deployment that you saw General Tolimir, as you mentioned in your previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, not that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us about when you did see General Tolimir, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When we went down to Zepa, up to a bridge, where there are four or five wooden huts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: How much time did you spend at that location you've just mentioned, the bridge where there are four or five wooden huts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Three days, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: What was your task or your unit's task during those three days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: To guard the bridge. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Describe the occasion or occasions when you saw General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was not really a personal encounter. I did not meet him as a person. He was passing by with his entourage in two vehicles of the VRS, two jeeps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Who else was in his entourage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: General Ratko Mladic was in one of the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And did you see any other officers from the VRS Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Not from the Main Staff, but there were officers of the Drina Corps who were there with their troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: During your time in the Zepa deployment, did you ever see the man Pecanac who you described in your previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I did not see him in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, right at the beginning of your testimony today, you recalled that yesterday you reviewed the interview statement from investigators from this office, and you confirmed that the contents of that statement were correct. And in that statement, sir, you describe in a little bit of detail the time in Zepa, and you also mention Mr. Pecanac. Would it help you to recall whether you saw Mr. Pecanac if you were to review what you said in that statement back in December of 2004?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't think Pecanac came to Zepa. I should look to see where.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, if it would help you to look --

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: -- then can I ask for the document to be put on screen. It's actually on the Defence list, so I understand that it is loaded up, and it's 65 ter 1D946. And the relevant page in both languages is page 4 in e-court. It's the bottom half of that page, if it can be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, if you just take a moment when the document is up on the screen to look at the paragraph you'll see numbered 11, and that's the paragraph in the statement where you describe the deployment to Zepa. It should come up on the left hand side of the screen in the Serbian language. Let us know if the text is big enough for you to read.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Pecanac was there for negotiations. When the negotiations started, when contact was made with Avdo Palic, also known as Professor, it's then that Pecanac and others from the security detail came. Our soldiers also went on the security detail. But that day when we came to the bridge and when we were there, he did not come to see us. He was passing by in the security detail of Mladic, but he did not really come to address us at the check-point while we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: So you say he was in the security detail of Mladic, does -- are you referring to the time when you say Tolimir and Mladic came by in two vehicles or are you referring to another time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That's a different occasion when contact was made with Avdo Palic to negotiate the surrender of Zepa. That's when Pecanac came, and our soldiers from the sabotage detachment went with him on his security detail to the location where the negotiations were held. But the first two days we were alone with our commander at the bridge. Nobody came to visit us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Now, how often during the whole of your Zepa deployment did you see General Tolimir or his vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see him personally. I just saw his vehicle pass by, the vehicles just passed by. We had no right to stop anybody. They were passing back and forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Was that on a single occasion or on more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: More than one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did any of your colleagues from the 10th Sabotage Detachment perform any protection duties for General Tolimir during the deployment in the Zepa area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, because General Mladic was also there. Perhaps they were protecting him, perhaps Tolimir. I don't know what they did, who they protected. I just saw them going to Zepa. They must have been on somebody's security detail, perhaps in another location. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did you see General Tolimir at the same time you saw Major Pecanac, or did you see them only on separate occasions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about what General Tolimir was doing in the Zepa area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That he was to negotiate with Avdo Palic, commander of the Zepa Brigade, about the surrender of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Were you in the Zepa area when the Muslim population left the enclave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I am not sure if the translation is working. Can you describe whether you saw the population leaving? Did you see buses? Did you see people gathered in groups? Can you describe, if you can remember, how you -- or what you saw?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Transport was provided for the population of Zepa, including buses. Without weapons, women and children were to come out first, then the wounded, then soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Were any soldiers from the Serb side escorting the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: There was the military police of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And when did you last see General Tolimir or General Tolimir's vehicle during your deployment to the Zepa area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That day when they were supposed to agree on the evacuation of the population of Zepa, when he finished those negotiations with Palic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, thank you very much. I don't have any further questions for you at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, now it's the turn of Mr. Tolimir to put questions to you during his cross-examination. Mr. Tolimir, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I hope this trial day ends in keeping with God's will, not mine. I would like to greet Mr. Elderkin whom I haven't seen in the courtroom in a long time. I would like to greet everyone else in the courtroom, including the witness and wish him welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Dragan, since we can we have speak the same language and this is to be interpreted, both my questions and your answers, let's try to make a brief pause between questions and answers so that they can follow, otherwise they don't be able to catch up and our questions and answers will overlap.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In your previous testimony in the Popovic case, you said you left Kladanj when the conflict in Bosnia started and from Kladanj you went to the territory of Republika Srpska. Could you please say whether that's correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And describe the circumstances how and why you left Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I left Kladanj in 1992, I believe it was in the month of May. I lived there before, I worked there, I had a house and family. And then the day came when I saw the units of the BH Army had come in, the Patriotic League, my family and I became suspicious. As soon as we saw those rifles, I thought I should take my family to a safer place, so I believe we left Kladanj in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Todorovic. Could you tell us whether you left your family house and everything and whether you returned after the war, and whether you left all the immovable and moveable property there that you couldn't take with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I had only one tracksuit and a pair of sneakers. The same goes for my wife and child. I left my house behind, all my property, and everything was burned down later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did the VRS do that or did the BH Army units do that waging war against the Serbian population?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, the BH Army came later. First of all, there was the Patriotic League and all the men who were creating problems before the war joined the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Maybe I wasn't clear. Did the VRS, after it was established, fight in Kladanj where your house was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at 1D946. That's your statement. It's already on the screen, in fact. We want to look at page 1, paragraph 4. More precisely, paragraph 2 in number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: It says that group in Bijeljina had the task to act behind enemy lines. And before that you said the sabotage detachment was linked to the security administration. So tell us, the sabotage units, including your detachment that were inserted into enemy territory, were they linked to the security administration or to the intelligence administration?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, my unit was subordinated to the Main Staff. Now, whether to intelligence or security, I don't know. The contract was with the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. If you don't know under which administration at the Main Staff you were, it doesn't matter. In any case, you were a member of the VRS and a member of the sabotage detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the course of the reading of this summary by Mr. Elderkin, he said at page 50, among other things -- in fact, he asked you when you entered the town and where your unit spent that first night. And you said you entered the town on the 11th and you spent the night near Srebrenica. That's what you said in your statement. I would like to know, did you arrive to Srebrenica from Zeleni Jadar without fighting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Then, before that, on the 11th, when you travelled, when did you journey from Zeleni Jadar to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: On the night of the 10th we spent the night near Srebrenica, or perhaps it was closer to Zeleni Jadar. I am not really sure about the geography. In any case, we came from the direction of Dragasevac, Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on the 10th, the night of the 10th, where you spent the night there, did you hear or see members of the 28th Division or had they already pulled out from the territory of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When we arrive at Srebrenica, there was still sporadic gun-fire, but there was no indication that there was any fighting. We were put up there, we spent the night, there was no combat, we didn't shoot, nobody shot at us. Occasionally, a round would be fired just to make it clear that there were troops around to mark the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you remember that night of the 10th and the 11th when you entered the area of Srebrenica after spending the night and entering the town, can you remember whether you saw any members of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: While entering Srebrenica, that morning when we got orders to go in, when we divided -- when we split into two groups, when we got order from our commander Pelemis who lined us up and gave us orders on how we are to act, how to be careful, that we shouldn't hurt anyone who voluntarily surrenders, that we should search houses in groups of three, we entered Srebrenica, perhaps it's a disgrace to say, but without firing a round.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Since you entered without firing a round, can we conclude based on your answers that you did not encounter any resistance when you entered the town of Srebrenica from Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: On the axis that our unit was, there was no combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: On page of an earlier transcript, that's the Popovic case, you said that you were guarding the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At the police station did you find anyone of the residents, Muslims, Serbs, or perhaps prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, you were asked a few questions about your time in Zepa during the combat for the liberation of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You indicated clearly on page 54 that you came, you passed by a house, and there was a UN APC next to that house, and you spent the whole day there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you engage in any combat in the area of Zepa at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In the questions and answers that followed concerning whom you had seen, et cetera, you said you were guarding a bridge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It was a very small river, the entrance into Zepa. There were some mills there and a few houses, four or five houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And you said then that you had seen officers pass by across that bridge towards Zepa, and you said you saw Tolimir and Mladic and also Pecanac. There was some question about Pecanac. My question is: Did you personally ever talk to Mladic, Tolimir, or Pecanac in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecutor asked you in this examination-in-chief whether you had seen residents of Zepa leaving Zepa for Kladanj. My question is: Did the residents of Zepa start leaving after the agreement was signed between the VRS and the BH Army on the evacuation of the population of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And we were very happy to see it end that way without casualties on either side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask: Based on your entire engagement in Srebrenica and Zepa, did you and the soldiers who were with you fight at all in Zepa or Srebrenica from the time when you came from Zeleni Jadar to the time when you came to Srebrenica, and later on the 20th of July to Zepa? Did anyone engage in any fighting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Todorovic, for all the answers you provided here during my examination. That was based on your statement and your earlier testimony. I have no further questions. Thank you for coming to this Court, for giving testimony. I wish you a pleasant journey and a safe return home. May God be with you and bless you. I hope you return safely to your family.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has completed its cross-examination of this witness. We have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge Mindua has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness Todorovic. Following up on the questions of General Tolimir, I would like one clarification. You entered Srebrenica on the 10th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 11th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for this clarification. Was your unit the first unit of the VRS to enter the enclave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was one of the first, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. Do you know if other VRS units had engaged in fighting against the 28th Division of the BH Army to take Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but not in the numbers that they tried to portray. In much smaller numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I didn't understand that really. What do you mean in much smaller numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant to say that there were troops of the VRS and the police there, but not in the numbers reported by reporters from Srebrenica. There were much fewer troops than they portrayed in the media, on TV, et cetera. Fewer troops were involved in the entry into Zepa than the Muslims said. They said 30.000 Serb soldiers attacked Srebrenica, and there was not even half that number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So according to you there were not 30.000 soldiers on the Serb side attacking Srebrenica, but I would like to understand this: This enclave of Srebrenica fell after a battle or battles with the 28th Division of the BH Army, or the town fell, as you've said, without a single bullet fired by the VRS without any resistance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My unit did not fire a single bullet. I am not saying there was no fighting anywhere on other sites.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I understand now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, you have used 1D946. That was the OTP statement of the witness. Are you tendering that document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It may be admitted. This is a Prosecution document that has been of use to us and may be of use to the Trial Chamber as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It may be admitted is not a clear answer. Are you tendering it or not? It's in your hands.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I said that I am tendering it because it can be used by all the sides in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D946 shall be assigned Exhibit D317. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it should be 318 because we have already a document with that number. D317 MFI'd is the document 1D951.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honours. Apologies. 1D946 shall be D318. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Elderkin, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours will be glad to hear that I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, you will be pleased to hear that this concludes already your examination in this trial. The Chamber would like to thank you that you were able to come to The Hague and to help us, and now you are free to return to your normal activities. Thank you very much, again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, is there another witness available for today?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'm afraid not, Your Honours. I believe the next group of witnesses are arriving over the weekend, so we have gone a little faster than we had expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed. We are in the same position. We have to adjourn for the week, and we will resume on Monday, 2.15 in this courtroom. We adjourn. I am very sorry. Everybody was already rising. I have to address the parties with one matter, very briefly. On the 8th of September we will have the videolink of one witness, and that probably start at 10.30 I was told by the registry, but we -- the relevant courtroom won't be available for us the whole day because there might be some technical problems. Please be aware that 10.30 we will start with that videolink conference. Sorry for this late notice. We adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of September, 2011, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.33 p.m.,
